ety.text: Inherited from Middle English upper. By surface analysis, up + -er.

senses.d: At a higher physical position, level, rank or order.
Situated on higher ground, further inland, more upstream, or more northerly.
Of or pertaining to a secondary school.
A stimulant, such as amphetamine, that increases energy and decreases appetite.

ex: These lines, GH and PC, are cut when the outline of the upper is cut out.

senses.d: The piece of material that forms the top part of a shoe or boot above the sole.
ex: genuine leather upper / balance manmade [label on a shoe]
Thus a vicious circle is established: the uppers offer participation, and the lowers, feeling persecuted, withdraw.

senses.d: That which is higher, contrasted with the lower.
ex: Next, take up slack equally on the two uppers until they are snug.
During the seventh week, the limbs also rotate laterally in the uppers and medially in the lowers.

senses.d: A tooth in the upper jaw.
ex: Periodically check the bite with the uppers and lowers to ensure that your actor's mouth will close correctly.

senses.d: A denture or retainer for the teeth in the upper jaw.
ex: The lower (according to the patient) was perfect, but the upper was bad, and the dentist was going to make the upper again.
The upper was retained with a Hawley bite plane; the lip bumper was continued for an additional 18 months.

senses.d: To fix an upper onto a shoe.
